title: Orbit database migrations must be run with make db-migrate, not alembic directly
body: In the Orbit monorepo `alembic upgrade head` run by hand connects to the `public` schema and skips the advisory lock, so it either creates tables in the wrong schema or races with the migration job in CI. Always run `make db-migrate ENV=local` (or `ENV=staging`), which sets `ORBIT_DB_SCHEMA=orbit_core`, takes `pg_advisory_lock(4242)` and then calls alembic from `services/core/migrations`.

title: Orbit api must never call the billing service synchronously; publish to the billing-events queue
body: After the 2024-03 incident where a slow billing deploy made every checkout request in `api` time out, direct HTTP calls from `api` to `billing` are forbidden and blocked by the `orbit/no-billing-http` lint rule. Publish a message with `publishBillingEvent()` from `packages/events` to the `billing-events` RabbitMQ queue and react to the `billing.settled` event instead of waiting for a response.

title: Orbit staging database is restored from an anonymized prod snapshot every night at 03:00 UTC
body: The `staging-db-restore` CronJob wipes the staging Postgres at 03:00 UTC and loads the anonymized production snapshot, so any test users, orders or tenants you created on staging disappear overnight. Put persistent test data in `scripts/staging-seed.sql`, which runs right after the restore, or use your own preview environment.

title: Orbit feature flags live in config/flags.yaml and only change with a deploy
body: The admin UI flag toggles were removed in 2025; the toggles still render but do nothing. Edit `config/flags.yaml` (per-environment sections `dev`, `staging`, `prod`), open a PR, and the change takes effect after the next deploy of the service that reads it. Read flags in code with `flags.isEnabled('name')` from `@orbit/flags` or `orbit_flags.is_enabled` in Python.

title: Orbit TypeScript API types are generated from the Python pydantic models with make contracts
body: Files in `packages/contracts/src/generated/` are produced from the pydantic schemas in `services/core/schemas` and must not be edited by hand. After changing a schema run `make contracts` and commit the regenerated files, otherwise the CI job `contracts-drift` fails with 'generated contracts are out of date'.

title: Orbit end-to-end tests only run on a PR when the run-e2e label is added
body: The Playwright suite in `apps/web/e2e` is expensive, so the `e2e.yml` GitHub Actions workflow is gated on the `run-e2e` label and is otherwise reported as skipped. Add the label before requesting review on any PR touching `apps/web` or `api`; merging to `main` is blocked until the e2e check is green.

title: Orbit per-PR preview environments live in namespace pr-<number> and are deleted after 72 hours
body: Every PR gets a preview deployment in the Kubernetes namespace `pr-<number>` at `https://pr-<number>.preview.orbit.dev`. The `preview-reaper` job deletes namespaces 72 hours after the last push, including their database. Push a new commit or comment `/preview extend` on the PR to keep it alive.

title: Orbit secrets come from Vault at secret/orbit/<service>, not from Kubernetes Secrets or .env in git
body: Kubernetes Secrets in Orbit are synced from Vault by the external-secrets operator and overwritten every 5 minutes, so editing them with kubectl is lost. Change values in Vault under `secret/orbit/<service>/<env>` and, for local development, run `orbit-cli secrets pull <service>` to write a git-ignored `.env.local`.

title: The Orbit monorepo uses pnpm workspaces; npm install creates a package-lock.json that CI rejects
body: Orbit is a pnpm 9 workspace (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`). Running `npm install` or `yarn` in any package creates a stray lockfile and breaks workspace links, and the `lockfile-guard` CI step fails on any `package-lock.json`. Use `corepack enable` and `pnpm install` from the repo root; add deps with `pnpm --filter <pkg> add <dep>`.

title: Every Orbit database query must go through TenantScopedSession to avoid leaking data between tenants
body: Postgres row-level security in Orbit relies on `SET app.tenant_id`, which only `TenantScopedSession` from `orbit_core.db` sets. A plain SQLAlchemy `Session()` runs without it and returns rows from all tenants in dev but nothing in prod, where RLS is enforced. Always use `with tenant_session(tenant_id) as s:`; the `orbit-no-raw-session` ruff plugin flags raw sessions.

title: Orbit production deploys are frozen from Friday 14:00 CET to Monday 08:00 CET
body: The `deploy-prod` workflow checks the freeze window and fails with 'deploy freeze active'. Re-running it will not help. For a real hotfix, get on-call approval and comment `/hotfix approve` on the release PR, which sets the `FREEZE_OVERRIDE` environment and lets the workflow proceed.

title: Orbit Python services are pinned to 3.11 because the reports service depends on a pinned pyarrow build
body: The `reports` service uses the internal `pyarrow==12.0.1+orbit` wheel that only exists for CPython 3.11, so bumping `.python-version` or the base image to 3.12 breaks `uv sync` with 'no matching distribution'. Keep 3.11 in `.python-version` and in `docker/python-base.Dockerfile` until ticket ORB-1187 replaces the wheel.

title: Orbit local dev Postgres listens on port 5433, not 5432
body: `make dev` starts the docker compose stack with Postgres mapped to host port 5433 so it does not clash with a locally installed Postgres. Tools that default to 5432 connect to the wrong server and report 'database orbit does not exist'. Use `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://orbit:orbit@localhost:5433/orbit` (already in `.env.example`) or `make psql`.

title: Orbit public API v1 is frozen; new fields and endpoints go only into v2
body: `/v1` endpoints are kept for legacy mobile clients and only receive security fixes; the `api-v1-freeze` CI check fails on any diff under `api/src/routes/v1`. Add new fields to the v2 serializers in `api/src/serializers/v2` and document them in `docs/api/v2.md`.

title: Long-running Orbit Celery tasks must be routed to the reports-slow queue
body: Workers on Orbit's `default` Celery queue have a 30 second soft time limit, so long exports are killed with `SoftTimeLimitExceeded` and retried forever. Decorate long tasks with `@orbit_task(queue='reports-slow')`, which runs on the `worker-slow` deployment with a 30 minute limit, and keep the default queue for short jobs.
